subject: PE & Wellbeing
source: National Curriculum (Physical Education); UK Chief Medical Officers' physical activity guidelines. Drive PE folder reviewed (TSS Long-Term PE Plan: fitness, fair play, leadership, resilience) and adapted to at-home, no-equipment, no-contact lessons.

lessons.title: Jumping and landing safely
objectives: Jump with two feet and land softly
Link two jumps in a sequence

keywords.def: to push off the ground with your feet
to come down after a jump
to make your knees go soft

starter: Bismillah. March on the spot for ten steps.

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Clear a space bigger than your jump
Wear non-slip shoes or bare feet on carpet
Rest if you feel dizzy or breathless
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: Two-foot jump
teach.note: Model slowly. Misconception: higher is better; control is better. Listen for quiet landings.

teach.heading: Jumping shapes
teach.note: Quarter turn is a small safe turn. Call out each shape. Keep turns small to avoid dizziness.

teach.heading: Jumping patterns
bullets: Jump side to side over an imaginary line
Make a pattern: two jumps, one clap
teach.note: Count together and keep a steady pace with claps.

practice: What do we do with our knees when we land?
independent: Do five jumps landing quietly each time.
Make a jump sequence: star, pencil, star.
exit: Create a sequence of three jumps and perform it twice.
Tell a grown-up why bent knees help.
lessons.send: Teach a family member your jump sequence.

lessons.title: Body shapes: tuck, star, straight
objectives: Make and name tuck, star and straight shapes

keywords.def: a wide shape with arms and legs apart
a long shape like a pencil

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Space to stretch your arms out
Stay on your feet or sit; no rolling
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: Three shapes
teach.note: Model while sitting or standing. Pupils copy and hold for three seconds.

teach.heading: Shapes on different parts
bullets: Straight lying down, or standing tall
teach.note: Lying down is optional. Check floor is clear and comfortable.

teach.heading: Link the shapes
bullets: Hop, then freeze in a star
Walk, then freeze in a tuck
Run on the spot, then straight
teach.note: Encourage control when stopping. Remind about tiny steps.

independent: Show tuck, star and straight, holding each for three seconds.
Travel for four steps and then freeze in a shape.
exit: Make a sequence: travel, shape, travel, shape.
homework: How do you hold a shape still?
lessons.send: Make three shapes with a family member and have them guess the names.
